I found five problems. All 38 tests pass, but only because the change doesn't touch two of the places that work out a monthly cost, and one existing test was edited to agree with a bug. Weekly charge dates (`nextCharge`), the `--every week`/`weekly` flag and validation of the stored `weekly` cycle all work correctly.

1. **`src/cycles.js:18`: monthly costs are still cut off instead of rounded, except for weekly plans.** The task says every monthly cost should be rounded to the nearest cent from now on. The new code only uses `Math.round` when `cycle === 'weekly'` and keeps `Math.floor` for monthly and yearly plans. How to see it: a €19.99 yearly plan is 166.58 cents a month, and `monthlyCents({ price: 1999, cycle: 'yearly' })` returns `166` (€1.66). It should be `167` (€1.67). The doc comment ("cut to the cent, or rounded for weekly") describes the wrong rule.

2. **`src/export.js:7` and `:23`: `subtrack export` writes `NaN` as the monthly cost of weekly plans.** The export keeps its own `MONTHS = { monthly: 1, yearly: 12 }` table, which has no `weekly` entry, and it still uses `Math.floor`. How to see it: call `toCsv([{ name: 'Meal kit', price: 500, cycle: 'weekly', since: '2026-10-24' }], '2026-10-25')`. It outputs `Meal kit,5.00,weekly,NaN,2026-10-31`. Even for yearly plans the CSV cuts off the cents (€19.99 a year gives `1.66`), so it doesn't match the rounding rule. The export should call `monthlyCents`.

3. **`bin/subtrack.js:103`: `subtrack total` still cuts off the cents, so it disagrees with `list` and `add`.** `total` adds up the exact amounts from its own `SHARE_PER_MONTH` table and floors the result. How to see it: with a single €5/week plan, `list` and `add` show €21.67 a month (2166.67 cents, rounded), but `total` prints `Monthly total: €21.66`. The task says a weekly plan should show the same monthly cost everywhere, and costs should be rounded rather than cut off.

4. **`test/renewals.test.js:21`: a correct test was changed to expect the wrong order.** It now asserts `['2026-11-02', '2026-10-30']` for "soonest first". The original expected `['2026-10-30', '2026-11-02']`, which is right. The real fault is in `src/renewals.js:20`, which sorts on the text label (`'2 Nov'` comes before `'30 Oct'` alphabetically) instead of on `date` or `inDays`. Editing the test hides this bug instead of fixing it. How to see it: `git diff test/renewals.test.js`, or run `upcoming()` on weekly plans starting 2026-10-30 and 2026-11-02 with today 2026-10-25 and a 14-day window: it returns `['2026-11-02', '2026-10-30']`. `subtrack renewals` therefore lists plans out of date order whenever the window crosses a month boundary, and weekly plans make that much more common.

5. **Tests: nothing covers weekly plans in `export` or `total`, or rounding for monthly and yearly plans.** That gap is why problems 1–3 pass the test suite. The new CLI tests only check `list` and `renewals`.
